findings.reason: Untrusted source: any locally generated or forwarded GSO skb handed to the IPoIB ndo_start_xmit. Save: ipoib_send() captures phead = skb->data at drivers/infiniband/ulp/ipoib/ipoib_ib.c:574 for skb_is_gso() skbs. Invalidating call: skb_linearize(skb) at ipoib_ib.c:595 (taken when skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags > usable_sge) can call pskb_expand_head, which allocates a new head, copies, and frees the old one for a cloned/non-linear skb. Unsafe use: the stale phead is passed to post_send(priv, ..., phead, hlen) at ipoib_ib.c:649 and stored as priv->tx_wr.header at ipoib_ib.c:554, so the HCA DMA-reads the header bytes from freed head memory. Counterevidence checked: when the skb is not cloned or already linear, skb_linearize does not reallocate and phead stays valid; the linearize branch also only runs for frag-heavy GSO skbs, so the bug is latent for typical traffic. Same mechanism as the seed (pointer into skb head used after a head-moving operation), on the TX rather than RX path.
findings.conclusion: ipoib_send saves phead=skb->data for GSO skbs, skb_linearize can pskb_expand_head-free the old head, and the stale phead is DMA-read by the HCA via tx_wr.header: stale-pointer use of freed head memory.

findings.reason: Untrusted source: FCoE frames arriving on any Ethernet interface registered for ethertype 0x8906 reach bnx2fc_recv_frame through the bnx2fc packet_type. Save: mac = eth_hdr(skb)->h_source and dest_mac = eth_hdr(skb)->h_dest at drivers/scsi/bnx2fc/bnx2fc_fcoe.c:536-537 alias the skb head. Invalidating call: pskb_trim(skb, fr_len) at bnx2fc_fcoe.c:555, where fr_len = skb->len - sizeof(struct fcoe_crc_eof) is attacker-influenced through the received frame length; for a cloned skb ___pskb_trim takes the pskb_expand_head path and frees the old head. Unsafe use: the stale mac/dest_mac are dereferenced at bnx2fc_fcoe.c:566 (ntoh24(&dest_mac[3])), :576 (ether_addr_equal(port->data_src_addr, dest_mac)) and :583 (ether_addr_equal(mac, ctlr->dest_addr)) - slab-use-after-free reads of freed head memory. Counterevidence checked: unlike the qedf twin (qedf_main.c:2315) there is no skb_linearize before the saves, so non-linear input is not ruled out; but on a never-cloned RX path pskb_trim keeps the old head and the pointers stay valid, hence medium not high confidence.
findings.conclusion: bnx2fc_recv_frame keeps eth_hdr()-derived mac/dest_mac across pskb_trim(skb, fr_len), which can pskb_expand_head-free the old head for a cloned FCoE frame, so the later dest_mac/mac comparisons read freed memory (stale-pointer UAF read).

findings.reason: Untrusted source: DVB network ULE SNDUs decoded from MPEG-TS payload bytes received by a DVB demux feed; the extension-header chain is attacker-chosen payload. Violated invariant: handle_ule_extensions() (dvb_net.c:266-280) sets p->ule_next_hdr = p->ule_skb->data and loops while ule_sndu_type < ETH_P_802_3_MIN, calling handle_one_ule_extension(); for an optional extension header hlen = (ule_sndu_type & 0x0700) >> 8 gives ext_len = hlen << 1 (0-14 bytes), and the loop advances p->ule_next_hdr += ext_len (dvb_net.c:254) and re-reads the next type word at p->ule_next_hdr-2 (:255) with no comparison of ule_next_hdr against p->ule_skb->len or skb_tail_pointer. The mandatory path has the same unbounded walk (:236, :238, :241). Unsafe use: bytes past the end of the ule_skb allocation are read and, after the loop, the total is consumed with skb_pull(h->priv->ule_skb, l) at dvb_net.c:721, so the resulting frame is built from out-of-bounds memory; the final total_ext_len is also unbounded versus the skb. Counterevidence checked: CRC32 verification of the SNDU runs before the extension walk (dvb_net_ule_check_crc), but the CRC is computed only over the received ule_skb bytes, so it does not bound ule_next_hdr; the linear-alloc ule_skb means the read runs past the end of a kmalloc slab rather than past skb_headlen.
findings.conclusion: handle_one_ule_extension walks p->ule_next_hdr through attacker-chosen optional/mandatory ULE extension headers with no bound against ule_skb->len, so type re-reads at dvb_net.c:255 read past the SNDU into adjacent slab memory (unbounded linear-area read).

candidates.reason: gdm_lte_multi_sdu_pkt (drivers/staging/gdm724x/gdm_lte.c:671-715) iterates num_packet (device-supplied u16) and for each SDU reads hci_len = sdu->len from the buffer, requires hci_len >= 12, then advances data += ((hci_len + 3) & 0xfffc) + HCI_HEADER_SIZE at line 712. The walk is driven entirely by the firmware-supplied multi-SDU buffer with no comparison of data or the accumulated offset against the buffer length passed in from gdm_lte_receive_pkt; the same holds for gdm_lte_netif_rx's DHCP chaddr read at gdm_lte.c:577-580 (addr = buf + iphdr + udphdr + offsetof(chaddr) with only len != 0 checked). Not fully traced to a conclusion because the phy_dev receive callbacks (gdm_usb/gdm_tty) were not audited before the finalize order.
candidates.conclusion: Follow up: confirm the upper bound (or absence) on the multi-SDU walk at gdm_lte.c:712 and the DHCP chaddr read at gdm_lte.c:577 by tracing phy_dev->rcv_func callers, to determine whether a malicious/compromised LTE modem firmware can read past the receive buffer.

candidates.reason: ssip_pn_rx() calls pskb_may_pull(skb, SSIP_MIN_PN_HDR) at drivers/hsi/clients/ssi_protocol.c:617 before any dereference of skb->data; the only pull-family call in the file, and the TX-side skb_cow_head(skb, 0) at :986 runs before the skb->data write with no pointer saved across it.

aoenet_rcv() already guarantees sizeof(aoe_hdr)+sizeof(aoe_atahdr) linear bytes via __pskb_pull_tail (drivers/block/aoe/aoenet.c:143-146) before handing the skb to aoecmd_ata_rsp; ktiocomplete() then derives hin/ahin from skb->data at aoecmd.c:1095-1097, and the skb_linearize(skb) at :1155 (ATA_CMD_ID_ATA) precedes its own skb->data use at :1158, with no pointer captured before it.

qedf_recv_frame() linearizes unconditionally (if (skb_is_nonlinear(skb)) skb_linearize(skb) at drivers/scsi/qedf/qedf_main.c:2314-2315) before capturing mac/dest_mac at :2315-2316, and only then runs pskb_trim(skb, fr_len) at :2336; after linearization the skb is uncloned so pskb_trim takes the __skb_trim fast path and the head is not reallocated.

In do_rx_iscsi_hdr/do_rx_iscsi_data the cpl header is read from skb->data at function entry and fully consumed by __skb_pull before __pskb_trim (drivers/scsi/cxgbi/cxgb4i/cxgb4i.c:1200-1201, :1307-1308); the only later skb->data use, bhs = skb->data at :1226, is re-derived after the trims, so no stale pointer crosses a head-moving call.

ctcm_unpack_skb() operates on ch->rx_skb built by dev_alloc_skb + skb_put in the driver, a fully linear driver-owned buffer; the header pointer at ctcm_main.c:81/107 is read from the linear area and each skb_pull/skb_put is guarded by skb_tailroom checks (:117, :170).

netiucv_unpack_skb() runs on conn->rx_buff, a linear alloc_skb(max_buffsize) buffer filled by iucv_message_receive (netiucv.c:1859, :695); header->next is bounded by the skb_tailroom check at netiucv.c:637 before skb_put, and msg->length is checked against max_buffsize at :682.

In fwnet_finish_incoming_packet the skb_pull(skb, sizeof(*eth)) at drivers/firewire/net.c:520 precedes the skb_mac_header(skb) cast; the payload is copied out of the firewire receive buffer into a fresh skb, and no pointer into the skb data area is saved across a reallocating call on the inspected path.

coverage_gaps: The ~20 remaining netif_rx/netif_receive_skb producers outside drivers/net that were only enumerated by grep (drivers/staging/most/net/net.c, drivers/staging/netlogic/xlr_net.c, drivers/staging/rtl*/ receive paths, drivers/message/fusion/mptlan.c, drivers/misc/sgi-xp/xpnet.c, drivers/infiniband/hw/hfi1/vnic_main.c, drivers/infiniband/hw/nes/nes_hw.c, drivers/isdn/i4l/isdn_net.c, drivers/isdn/hysdn/hysdn_net.c, drivers/staging/ks7010/ks_hostif.c) were not read to a conclusion before the finalize order.

Bluetooth HCI transport parsers (drivers/bluetooth/hci_bcsp.c, hci_ll.c, hci_nokia.c, btmtkuart.c:874, btmtksdio.c:267, btrsi.c:68) and the drivers/nfc HCI/NCI client parsers (st21nfca dep.c/se.c/core.c, st-nci, port100.c, trf7970a.c) were scanned for skb->data/skb_pull/trim patterns but no per-function stale-pointer audit was completed in this session.

No runtime confirmation (KASAN build, reproducer, or compile) was possible against this read-only snapshot; all three findings rest on source reading of the exact save/invalidating-call/use lines and on the pskb_expand_head/___pskb_trim/alloc_skb semantics read in this tree.
limitations: All three findings are source-reading hypotheses, not reproductions: no build, KASAN run or crafted packet was executed, and for the two skb-head findings the head reallocation is inferred from pskb_expand_head's alloc-copy-free of the old head and ___pskb_trim's skb_cloned() branch rather than observed.

The ipoib finding is a TX-path variant: it needs a GSO skb with nr_frags > usable_sge that is still cloned or non-linear when skb_linearize runs, the stale read is performed by the HCA DMA engine through tx_wr.header, and the observable failure is a malformed header/I/O error rather than a KASAN splat.

The bnx2fc finding requires the received FCoE frame's skb to be cloned (e.g. by an AF_PACKET tap or GRO) when pskb_trim runs and its length to exceed fr_len; on a never-cloned receive path the stale mac/dest_mac still alias valid memory and the issue is latent, hence medium confidence.

The dvb_net ULE finding's attacker is the DVB feed content (broadcast stream or malicious mux): the OOB read is from the linear ule_skb allocation rather than past skb_headlen, so it is an adjacent-slab read of at most ~16 bytes per extension-header step unless the unbounded loop accumulates further; triggering requires CONFIG_DVB_NET plus an attached ULE feed.

Non-linearity and cloning preconditions for the reported sites were assessed structurally (eth_type_trans/GRO/tap cloning behavior), not by a per-driver runtime audit of which s05 configurations actually deliver such skbs.

Snapshot revision is opaque (no git history or network permitted); line numbers are valid only for snapshots/s05 as supplied, and net/phonet/pep.c pep_get_sb was excluded by assignment rule and never reported.
